subject: Does Rqtl only ouput in cM?

messages.author: acb750e476c0ff5d
messages.subject: Does Rqtl only ouput in cM?
parts:
When I run Rqtl the output is in cM. Is there any option for bp or Mbp? My incoming data is GigaMUGA data with a SNP map with marker positions in bp. Does Rqtl convert this to cM? I've read in the discussion group about getting positions into cM. If left in bp memory problems can occur for calc.genoprob with a step equal to 1. Rqtl tries to insert psuedomarkers between every bp. I did have this problem. Is it ok to set the step equal to 0? I've done that and get results. I was told that I need QTL results in bp or Mbp for publication. What is the best way to get that?

Thanks

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Does Rqtl only ouput in cM?
parts:
For calculation of genotype probabilities, the marker positions need to be in cM. With very dense markers it probably doesn't much matter, but basepairs is generally not what you want, and if you say step=1 in calc.genoprob when you have a map in basepairs, you're asking for all calculations to be performed every basepair, and that why you'll have memory issues. If you use step=0 it does calculations just at the markers.

I would at least convert to Mbp rather than bp. And then for the mouse genome, you could divide by 2 to get a rough estimate of cM. Better would be to use a mouse genetic map, for which the "mouse map converter" tool is useful: http://cgd.jax.org/mousemapconverter

If you need to get positions back to Mbp, you could either focus solely on the marker positions, whose Mbp positions you already know, or you can use interpPositions() to interpolate between the genetic and physical maps, and replacemap() to replace genetic map positions with physical positions.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Does Rqtl only ouput in cM?
parts:
Karl,

Thanks for the help. I'm using argyle to sort and filter my data. Argyle uses the R probes file from UNC. Andrew pointed out to me that it includes both genetic and physical positions. I didn't realize that. The SNP map file that is included with GigaMUGA data only has bp positions. Argyle sends the cM positions to Rqtl for the genotype probabilities calculations. Based on that I should be good on the front end of things.

The only thing I should need to do then is use replacemap() to swap out the genetic map positions with the physical positions from the UNC probes file (snps.gigamuga.Rdata).

Thanks,
Bill
